data.cycle_day: The billing cycle starts on day

data_description.consumption_entity: The meter accumulating the kWh bought from the grid. It needs long-term statistics: they are read hour by hour.
data_description.export_entity: Only if you have panels. Leave it empty otherwise.
data_description.cycle_day: Check the start date on your last bill. Usually the 1st.

power.name: Contracted power
power.description: Charged every day of the month whether you use it or not. The 2.0TD tariff has two power periods and you can contract a different figure for each.

data_description.power_p1_kw: The P1 figure on your contract. A home is usually between 3.3 and 5.75 kW.
data_description.power_p1_price: On the bill it reads «potencia punta», in euros per kW and day.
data_description.power_p2_kw: The P2 figure. Usually the same as peak.
data_description.power_p2_price: Considerably cheaper than peak: about a quarter of it.

pricing.title: How your energy is priced
pricing.description: What we ask next depends on this answer. If you are not sure, look at the prices section of your contract: either there is a single price per kWh, or a table of three, or none at all because it changes every hour.

data.energy_flat: I pay the same at every hour (flat rate)

data_description.energy_flat: Untick this if your tariff has time-of-use pricing, that is, a different price at peak (P1), mid-peak (P2) and off-peak (P3).
data_description.energy_source: If an entity publishes it, you pick which one in the next step. With time-of-use pricing you are asked for one entity per period, which is how some retailers publish them.

energy.title: Energy price
energy.description: Prices per kWh WITHOUT taxes, as they appear on the contract.

data.energy_price_taxed: That entity gives the price with taxes included

data_description.energy_price: What you pay for each kWh bought. If your tariff has periods, this is peak (P1): weekdays 10-14 and 18-22.
data_description.energy_price_p3: Nights, weekends and national holidays, all day.
data_description.energy_price_entity: Its hourly statistics are read, not its current value: a bill is built from the price that applied while the energy flowed. On a flat tariff this is the only entity needed.
data_description.energy_price_entity_p2: Time-of-use tariffs only: the entity publishing the mid-peak price.
data_description.energy_price_entity_p3: Time-of-use tariffs only: the off-peak one.
data_description.energy_price_taxed: Tick this if the entity already includes the electricity tax and VAT; they will be stripped before computing, or every kWh would be taxed twice. The Octopus one, for instance, includes them.

surplus.title: What comes back from your panels
surplus.description: No panels? Submit without changing anything.

data.surplus_price_taxed: That entity gives the price with taxes included
data.surplus_capped: Surplus cannot exceed the energy term
data.hourly_netting: Net consumption against export within each hour

data_description.surplus_price: What you are credited per kWh exported. Leave it at 0 if you do not export.
data_description.surplus_price_entity: Only if your compensation varies by the hour too.
data_description.surplus_price_taxed: Careful: it may differ from the purchase one. At Octopus the purchase price carries taxes and the surplus price does not.
data_description.battery_entity: The pot where surplus with nothing left to cancel out accumulates in euros: Solar Wallet at Octopus, Solar Cloud at Iberdrola. Its balance is applied at the end, after tax, and can take a bill to zero but never below.
data_description.surplus_capped: That is the rule: compensation can take the energy term to zero but never into your favour. What is left goes to the virtual battery, if you have one.
data_description.hourly_netting: The hourly net balance Spanish law requires: export 3 kWh and import 1 in the same hour and it counts as having exported 2. Leave it ticked unless you know your retailer does otherwise.

extras.title: Charges, services and taxes
extras.description: Everything that does not depend on what you consume. The taxes come filled in with the rates in force in Spain; you only need to touch them if they change.

regulated.name: Regulated charges
regulated.description: Set by the government and identical for everyone. Look them up on a bill once and never think about them again.

data_description.meter_rental: Renting the meter, around €0.027 a day.

retailer.name: What your retailer charges
retailer.description: This is where two bills on the same tariff stop looking alike: add-on services under whatever name each retailer gives them, and the discounts that usually come attached.

data_description.monthly_fee: Maintenance, home packs, call-out cover — whatever they bill you monthly beside the electricity itself.
data_description.monthly_fee_name: How it should read in the breakdown. For example, «Pack Hogar».
data_description.discount_percent: The percentage taken off the energy term. It is computed on the undiscounted energy and shows up in the taxes too, because you are taxed on what you are charged.
data_description.discount_name: For example, «Plan Estable». Left empty it reads as «Discount».

taxes.name: Taxes
taxes.description: The values filled in are the ones in force in Spain.

data.tax_includes_bono: The bono social counts towards the electricity-tax base

data_description.tax_includes_bono: Retailers differ here: Iberdrola includes it, Octopus does not. Check your bill, in the base they compute the electricity tax on.
